maya (sec-eng): FYI: customers in APAC reporting intermittent TLS errors to model endpoints after yesterday's regional hardening rollout. Error patterns look like "unexpected_message" during handshake.
kumar (infra): Which region? ap-south or ap-southeast? We did a config push to both.
maya (sec-eng): Mostly ap-southeast but a handful in ap-south too. Logs show: client offered TLS1.2 + RSA-only suites and server dropped connection.
liam (edge): We tightened ciphers to ECDHE-only globally two days ago. The canary in apac passed, but looks like some older device fleet still requires RSA.
opsbot: incident created: #INC-2026-4911 region=apac severity=medium-availability
audit-bot: Noted rotation/hardening event: cfgpush-20260319-1845; actor=infra-deploy-bot.
kumar (infra): Two things to confirm: 1) Did the cert rotator rotate any keys/aliases in apac keystore? 2) Any IAM denies for kms:Decrypt when services attempted to load certs?
maya (sec-eng): I scanned cloudtrail: rotator job touched secrets in apac at 18:46 with alias update. Also found one KMS AccessDenied at 18:47 for arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:...:key/abc123 when edge-service tried to hot-reload.
liam (edge): Hot-reload failed, fallback to existing cert expired? We had code that if hot-reload fails it drops connections for a minute while retrying. Oops.
maya (sec-eng): Proposed quick fixes: 1) re-add RSA-AES fallback on LB only in apac behind a canary flag, 2) grant edge-service kms:Decrypt for the new key arn with condition on aws:RequestedRegion, 3) revert global ECDHE-only until we have client telemetry.
kumar (infra): I'll open an IAM PR scoped to ap-southeast-1 and ap-south-1 and add the specific key ARN to edge-service role. Will include CloudTrail evidence in PR.
liam (edge): For the canary, I'll target 5% of apac backends and add a short lived feature flag. Nginx snippet: 
```
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
  ssl_ciphers "ECDHE+AESGCM:ECDHE+CHACHA20:RSA+AES:!aNULL:!MD5";
}
```
opsbot: canary deploy started (deploy_id=canary-5170000123-1) 5% apac backends
maya (sec-eng): Also: let's track client IPs and TLS ClientHello fingerprints into the telemetry pipeline so product can contact affected customers. Add an eval to rotation job: verify IAM access to all keystore keys in regions targeted before finalizing rotation.
kumar (infra): PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/iam/pull/441 (adds kms:Decrypt for key abc123, condition aws:RequestedRegion=ap-southeast-1). Tagging @sec-eng for signoff.
audit-bot: Manual approval logged: "kumar approved edge-service kms:Decrypt for key abc123 in ap-southeast-1". Audit-ID=aud-5170000123-1
liam (edge): Canary reduced errors for flagged IPs. Still seeing a small percentage from a legacy client library that uses TLS1.0 fallback.
maya (sec-eng): TLS1.0 clients are out of scope; we need to notify customers. For this incident, limit fallback to TLS1.2+RSA only. Do not enable TLS1.0.
kumar (infra): Understood. I'll merge the PR with region condition and short TTL on the allowance (remove in 48h unless escalation).
liam (edge): Rolling fallback to 25% now; monitoring dashboards show handshake error rate dropping.
opsbot: monitor:tls-handshakes-apac suppressed due to canary.
maya (sec-eng): Post-incident actions: 1) Add per-region IAM validation step to cert rotation; 2) Add telemetry for ClientHello cipher set frequency; 3) Create customer outreach template for legacy TLS clients.
kumar (infra): I'll include the IAM validation as a gate in rotator pipeline and add CloudTrail diff output in rotation job artifacts.
liam (edge): We'll remove RSA fallback after 24h and confirm no new hits.
maya (sec-eng): Thanks team. If anything spikes, escalate to Sev2. Will prepare a short write-up for the weekly security sync. :thumbsup:
